ports.name: core_rsp_o.data
ports.functionality: Forms the core data from the system data with bit0 replaced by (sys data bit0 OR sc_fail); the upper bits are forwarded from sys_rsp_i.data(31 downto 1).
ports.evidence: core_rsp_o.data <= sys_rsp_i.data(31 downto 1) & (sys_rsp_i.data(0) or sc_fail); concurrent concat/assign

ports.name: sys_req_o
ports.functionality: Emits a system bus request derived from core_req_i; starts as a record copy of core_req_i then conditionally alters the stb field for AMO writes.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; then sys_req_o.stb overwritten conditionally

ports.name: sys_req_o.addr
ports.functionality: Carries the core request address into the system request unchanged (copied from core_req_i by bus_request).
ports.evidence: bus_request: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; copies addr field

ports.name: sys_req_o.data
ports.functionality: Carries the core request data into the system request unchanged via the record copy, subject to the subsequent stb modification.
ports.evidence: bus_request: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; copies data field

ports.name: sys_req_o.ben
ports.functionality: Forwards the core byte-enable bits to the system request via the record copy in the bus_request process.
ports.evidence: bus_request: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; copies ben field

ports.name: sys_req_o.stb
ports.functionality: Is assigned from core_req_i.stb but, for AMO write operations, is gated with state(1) to control when the system sees the strobe.
ports.evidence: bus_request: if (rvso='1') and (core_req_i.rw='1') then sys_req_o.stb <= core_req_i.stb and state(1) else sys_req_o.stb <= core_req_i.stb

ports.name: sys_req_o.rw
ports.functionality: Carries the read/write indicator from core_req_i into the system request via the record copy in bus_request.
ports.evidence: bus_request: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; copies rw field

ports.name: sys_req_o.src
ports.functionality: Forwards the source field from the core request into the system request by record copy.
ports.evidence: bus_request: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; copies src field

ports.name: sys_req_o.priv
ports.functionality: Forwards the priv flag from core_req_i into sys_req_o via the record copy.
ports.evidence: bus_request: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; copies priv field

ports.name: sys_req_o.debug
ports.functionality: Forwards the debug flag from the core request into the system request by record copy.
ports.evidence: bus_request: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; copies debug field

ports.name: sys_req_o.amo
ports.functionality: Carries the AMO indicator from the core request into sys_req_o via the record copy in bus_request.
ports.evidence: bus_request: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; copies amo field

ports.name: sys_req_o.amoop
ports.functionality: Forwards the AMO opcode bits from the core request into the system request by record copy in bus_request.
ports.evidence: bus_request: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; copies amoop field

ports.name: sys_req_o.lock
ports.functionality: Forwards the lock flag from core_req_i into sys_req_o through the record copy in bus_request.
ports.evidence: bus_request: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; copies lock field

ports.name: sys_req_o.fence
ports.functionality: Forwards the fence flag from the core request into sys_req_o by record copy in bus_request.
ports.evidence: bus_request: sys_req_o <= core_req_i; copies fence field

ports.name: sys_rsp_i
ports.functionality: Receives the system response record; its fields feed core response outputs and drive FSM transition on ack.
ports.evidence: core_rsp_o fields assigned from sys_rsp_i.*; sys_rsp_i.ack used in rvs_control

ports.name: sys_rsp_i.ack
ports.functionality: Indicates system acknowledgment; it gates FSM transition out of wait state and contributes to core_rsp_o.ack.
ports.evidence: rvs_control: when "11" if (sys_rsp_i.ack = '1') then state <= "00"; and core_rsp_o.ack <= sys_rsp_i.ack or sc_fail

ports.name: sys_rsp_i.err
ports.functionality: Delivers the system error status and is forwarded unchanged to core_rsp_o.err.
ports.evidence: core_rsp_o.err  <= sys_rsp_i.err; concurrent direct assignment

ports.name: sys_rsp_i.data
ports.functionality: Provides the 32-bit data from system; its upper 31 bits and bit0 are used to form core_rsp_o.data with bit0 ORed with sc_fail.
ports.evidence: core_rsp_o.data <= sys_rsp_i.data(31 downto 1) & (sys_rsp_i.data(0) or sc_fail)

signals.name: state
signals.functionality: Holds the arbiter state (S_IDLE, S_BUSY_A, S_BUSY_B); updated from state_nxt on clock edges and used as the case selector in combinational FSM.
signals.evidence: state <= state_nxt on rising_edge(clk_i) (arbiter_sync); case state is ... in arbiter_fsm

signals.name: state_nxt
signals.functionality: Combinationally computed next state based on current state, sticky requests, incoming stb/locks, sel_q and x_rsp_i.ack; then captured into state at the clock edge.
signals.evidence: state_nxt assigned in arbiter_fsm case branches using a_req/b_req/a_req_i.stb/b_req_i.stb/sel_q/locked/x_rsp_i.ack

signals.name: a_req
signals.functionality: Captures and holds that A has requested (a_req_i.stb) until the arbiter services A; cleared when state is S_BUSY_A or on reset.
role: holds pending A request across cycles
signals.evidence: a_req <= '0' on reset or when state = S_BUSY_A else a_req <= a_req or a_req_i.stb (arbiter_sync clocked)

signals.name: b_req
signals.functionality: Captures and holds that B has requested (b_req_i.stb) until the arbiter services B; cleared when state is S_BUSY_B or on reset.
role: holds pending B request across cycles
signals.evidence: b_req <= '0' on reset or when state = S_BUSY_B else b_req <= b_req or b_req_i.stb (arbiter_sync clocked)

signals.name: sel
signals.functionality: Combinationally chosen by arbiter_fsm to indicate which port (A='0' or B='1') is granted; used to multiplex x_req_o fields and to route responses to the selected client.
signals.evidence: sel assigned in arbiter_fsm branches; used in many when (sel = '0') else ... assignments; sel_q <= sel on rising_edge(clk_i)

signals.name: sel_q
signals.functionality: Registered copy of sel captured on clock edge; used in arbitration decisions (ROUND_ROBIN_EN logic) to bias the next selection.
signals.evidence: sel_q <= sel in arbiter_sync; used in arbiter_fsm: if (sel_q = '1') or (not ROUND_ROBIN_EN) then ...

signals.name: stb
signals.functionality: Combinational signal indicating when a transfer should be issued; computed by arbiter_fsm and forwarded directly to x_req_o.stb.
signals.evidence: stb set in arbiter_fsm branches (stb <= '1' in grant branches; stb <= a_req_i.stb/b_req_i.stb in locked branches); x_req_o.stb <= stb

signals.name: locked
signals.functionality: Two-bit register holding the latched lock bits (from A and B) captured from locked_nxt at clock edges; each bit gates busy-branch behavior when set.
signals.evidence: locked <= locked_nxt on rising_edge(clk_i); locked(0)/locked(1) tested in S_BUSY_A/S_BUSY_B branches to control stb and state_nxt

signals.name: locked_nxt
signals.functionality: Combinationally computed next locked value as b_req_i.lock & a_req_i.lock in idle branch or preserved otherwise; fed into locked on clock.
signals.evidence: locked_nxt <= b_req_i.lock & a_req_i.lock in others branch; default locked_nxt <= locked

signals.name: port_sel
signals.functionality: Combinational vector where each bit indicates whether req_i.addr matches a configured base or X acts as fallback; used to gate per-port strobes.
signals.evidence: concurrent when assignments set port_sel(0..3) from A_EN/B_EN/C_EN/X_EN and req_i.addr; request process uses port_sel(i); bus_monitor assigns keeper.halt<=port_sel(port_sel'left).

signals.name: port_req
signals.functionality: Combinational array built in the request process: each element is either a terminated request or a copy of req_i with its stb gated by port_sel, and is forwarded to the corresponding external req_o port.
signals.evidence: request process: for i loop sets port_req(i)<=req_terminate_c or port_req(i)<=req_i and port_req(i).stb<=port_sel(i) and req_i.stb; concurrent assigns map port_req(n) to a_req_o/b_req_o/...

signals.name: port_rsp
signals.functionality: Mirrors external per-port response inputs (port_rsp(i)<=a_rsp_i/b_rsp_i/...) and supplies those fields to the response aggregation process which builds int_rsp.
signals.evidence: concurrent assignments: port_rsp(0)<=a_rsp_i ... port_rsp(3)<=x_rsp_i; response process reads port_rsp(i) to build tmp_v assigned to int_rsp.

signals.name: int_rsp
signals.functionality: Holds the OR-aggregated data/ack/err results from enabled port_rsp entries computed in the response process and then drives rsp_o assignments and bus_monitor checks.
signals.evidence: response process builds tmp_v by ORing port_rsp(i) fields then int_rsp<=tmp_v; int_rsp used in rsp_o assignments and bus_monitor checks int_rsp.ack.

signals.name: int_rsp.ack
signals.functionality: Is the OR of port_rsp(i).ack for enabled ports and is used both to drive rsp_o.ack and to clear keeper.busy when seen.
signals.evidence: response process ORs port_rsp(i).ack into tmp_v.ack assigned to int_rsp; bus_monitor uses (int_rsp.ack='1') to clear keeper.busy; rsp_o.ack<=int_rsp.ack or keeper.err.

signals.name: int_rsp.err
signals.functionality: Is the OR of port_rsp(i).err for enabled ports and contributes to the external rsp_o.err output.
signals.evidence: response process ORs port_rsp(i).err into tmp_v.err assigned to int_rsp; rsp_o.err<=int_rsp.err or keeper.err.

signals.name: int_rsp.data
signals.functionality: Is the bitwise-OR aggregation of port_rsp(i).data fields and is forwarded unchanged to rsp_o.data.
signals.evidence: response process: tmp_v.data := tmp_v.data or port_rsp(i).data; int_rsp<=tmp_v; rsp_o.data<=int_rsp.data.

signals.name: keeper
signals.functionality: Registers busy, lock, timeout counter, err and halt flags; updated on reset and clock edges in bus_monitor reacting to req_i, port_sel and int_rsp to implement timeout and completion behavior.
signals.evidence: bus_monitor process assigns keeper fields on reset and on rising_edge(clk_i); keeper.err used in rsp_o assignments and keeper.halt<=port_sel(...).

signals.name: keeper.busy
signals.functionality: Indicates an ongoing transaction; is set from req_i.stb when idle and cleared on ack, lock release or timeout inside the clocked bus_monitor process.
signals.evidence: bus_monitor: if (keeper.busy='0') then keeper.busy<=req_i.stb; else ... keeper.cnt reset when busy='0'.

signals.name: keeper.lock
signals.functionality: Records the lock bit from the request when busy starts and is consulted together with req_i.lock to determine forced completion of the transaction.
signals.evidence: bus_monitor: when keeper.busy='0' then keeper.lock<=req_i.lock; completion checks (keeper.lock='1') and (req_i.lock='0').

signals.name: keeper.cnt
signals.functionality: Counts clock cycles while keeper.busy is '1' by incrementing itself; is reset to zero when keeper.busy is '0' to implement TIMEOUT detection.
signals.evidence: bus_monitor: keeper.cnt <= (others=>'0') when busy='0' else keeper.cnt<=std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(keeper.cnt)+1); timeout check uses keeper.cnt(msb).

signals.name: keeper.err
signals.functionality: Is set when the timeout counter overflows while not halted, cleared at each clock cycle start, and contributes to external rsp_o.ack and rsp_o.err via ORing.
signals.evidence: bus_monitor sets keeper.err<='1' when keeper.cnt(msb)='1' and keeper.halt='0'; rsp_o.ack/err <= int_rsp.* or keeper.err.

signals.name: keeper.halt
signals.functionality: Captures the current top port_sel bit (port_sel'left) on clock and inhibits timeout escalation when asserted; used in the timeout condition evaluation.
signals.evidence: bus_monitor: keeper.halt <= port_sel(port_sel'left); timeout check uses (keeper.halt='0') to set keeper.err.

signals.name: dev_req
signals.functionality: Array of per-device request records. Each element is produced by a per-device generator from main_req (with stb gated by address match) for enabled devices or assigned req_terminate_c when disabled; each element drives the corresponding dev_X_req_o port.
signals.evidence: bus_request process: dev_req(i) <= main_req; and concurrent assignments dev_29_req_o <= dev_req(29); etc.

signals.name: dev_rsp
signals.functionality: Array collecting responses from all devices. Each dev_rsp(i) is assigned from the corresponding dev_x_rsp_i input port and then read by the bus_response process which ORs fields into the aggregated main_rsp.
role: signal vector driven by device response ports
signals.evidence: Concurrent assignments dev_rsp(i) <= dev_x_rsp_i; bus_response process ORs dev_rsp(i).data/ack/err and assigns main_rsp <= tmp_v.

signals.name: main_req
signals.functionality: Signal carrying the main/host request provided by the instantiated bus register (neorv32_bus_reg_inst.device_req_o). It is used as the source for per-device generators (dev_req(i) <= main_req) and its address bits are compared to device bases.
signals.evidence: Instance port map: device_req_o => main_req; and bus_request process uses main_req and assigns dev_req(i) <= main_req;

signals.name: main_req.addr
signals.functionality: Address slice of the main request used to select which device's stb is asserted. The addr range main_req.addr(addr_hi_c downto addr_lo_c) is compared with each device base to gate dev_req(i).stb.
signals.evidence: Comparison in bus_request process: if (main_req.addr(addr_hi_c downto addr_lo_c) = dev_base_list_c(i)(addr_hi_c downto addr_lo_c)) then dev_req(i).stb <= main_req.stb;

signals.name: main_req.data
signals.functionality: Data field of the main request record. It is forwarded (as part of the record) into each dev_req(i) when assigned from main_req so devices may receive the data.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req; (bus_request process uses main_req as source)

signals.name: main_req.ben
signals.functionality: Byte-enable field forwarded from main_req into per-device dev_req(i) assignments so device receives correct byte-enable signals.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req; (bus_request process uses main_req fields)

signals.name: main_req.stb
signals.functionality: Valid/strobe bit from the main request. It is propagated into dev_req(i).stb when the address matches; otherwise dev_req(i).stb is driven '0'.
signals.evidence: In bus_request process: dev_req(i) <= main_req; and dev_req(i).stb <= main_req.stb when address matches

signals.name: main_req.rw
signals.functionality: Read/write flag from the main request. It is forwarded into dev_req(i) when dev_req(i) is assigned from main_req so devices learn operation type.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req; (bus_request process uses main_req fields)

signals.name: main_req.src
signals.functionality: Source identifier field of the main request forwarded into per-device requests when dev_req(i) <= main_req executes.
role: supplies source id to per-device requests
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req; (bus_request process)

signals.name: main_req.priv
signals.functionality: Privilege bit from the main request forwarded into dev_req(i) when the per-device assignment executes.
role: supplies privilege flag to per-device requests
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req; (bus_request process)

signals.name: main_req.debug
signals.functionality: Debug bit of the main request forwarded into per-device requests as part of the record assignment dev_req(i) <= main_req.
role: supplies debug flag to per-device requests
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req; (bus_request process)

signals.name: main_req.amo
signals.functionality: Atomic-operation indicator forwarded into each dev_req(i) by the per-device assignment from main_req.
role: supplies AMO flag to per-device requests
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req; (bus_request process)

signals.name: main_req.amoop
signals.functionality: AMO opcode forwarded from main_req into dev_req(i) during the per-device assignment so devices receive AMO operation code.
role: supplies AMO opcode to per-device requests
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req; (bus_request process)

signals.name: main_req.lock
signals.functionality: Lock bit forwarded from the main request into per-device dev_req when assigned, so devices receive lock information.
role: supplies lock flag to per-device requests
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req; (bus_request process)

signals.name: main_req.fence
signals.functionality: Fence bit forwarded from main_req into per-device requests as part of the record assignment that produces dev_req(i).
role: supplies fence flag to per-device requests
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req; (bus_request process)

signals.name: main_rsp
signals.functionality: Aggregated response to the host: bus_response process ORs enabled dev_rsp entries into a temporary variable and assigns it to main_rsp, which is connected to the bus register instance's device_rsp_i port.
role: aggregated response source for host register
signals.evidence: bus_response process ORs dev_rsp(i) into tmp_v and then main_rsp <= tmp_v; instance port map: device_rsp_i => main_rsp;

signals.name: main_rsp.ack
signals.functionality: Aggregated acknowledgement bit produced by OR-ing dev_rsp(i).ack across enabled devices in the bus_response process and assigned into main_rsp.ack.
signals.evidence: bus_response process: tmp_v.ack := tmp_v.ack or dev_rsp(i).ack; then main_rsp <= tmp_v;

signals.name: main_rsp.err
signals.functionality: Aggregated error bit formed by OR-ing dev_rsp(i).err across enabled devices inside the bus_response process and assigned to main_rsp.err.
signals.evidence: bus_response process: tmp_v.err := tmp_v.err or dev_rsp(i).err; then main_rsp <= tmp_v;

signals.name: main_rsp.data
signals.functionality: Aggregated data word computed by OR-ing dev_rsp(i).data across enabled devices in the bus_response process and written into main_rsp.data.
signals.evidence: bus_response process: tmp_v.data := tmp_v.data or dev_rsp(i).data; then main_rsp <= tmp_v;

signals.name: arbiter
signals.function: holds AMO FSM state and data
signals.functionality: Register record that stores the FSM state, AMO opcode and read/write data. It captures arbiter_nxt on the clock and is reset to defaults.
role: provides control and operands to combinational logic
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt on rising_edge(clk_i); reset branch sets arbiter fields in arbiter_sync

signals.name: arbiter.state
signals.functionality: Holds the current AMO FSM state; it is captured from arbiter_nxt at clock and is used as the case selector and in conditional expressions to choose outputs and next-state updates.
signals.evidence: case arbiter.state is in arbiter_comb; many concurrent assigns use (arbiter.state = ...) conditions

signals.name: arbiter.cmd
signals.functionality: Stores the AMO opcode captured from arbiter_nxt; its low bits select the ALU operation and bit 3 controls signed/unsigned handling in compare operands.
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt capture; case arbiter.cmd(2 downto 0) in amo_alu; arbiter.cmd(3) used in cmp_opa/cmp_opb

signals.name: arbiter.rdata
signals.functionality: Holds the read data sampled from sys_rsp_i (captured via arbiter_nxt.rdata) and supplies operands for ALU and response routing back to the core.
role: provides operand to ALU and core response
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt capture; arbiter_nxt.rdata <= sys_rsp_i.data in S_READ_WAIT; arbiter.rdata used in amo_alu and core_rsp_o.data

signals.name: arbiter.wdata
signals.functionality: Stores the write data from the core captured into arbiter_nxt.wdata when an AMO begins and supplies it as an ALU operand.
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt capture; arbiter_nxt.wdata <= core_req_i.data in S_IDLE; arbiter.wdata used in amo_alu and cmp_opb

signals.name: arbiter_nxt
signals.functionality: Aggregates the combinationally computed next FSM state, opcode and data (arbiter_nxt.*). It is derived from current arbiter, core request fields and system responses and then sampled into arbiter on the clock.
signals.evidence: arbiter_nxt <= arbiter default and case arbiter.state assigns arbiter_nxt fields in arbiter_comb; arbiter_sync captures arbiter_nxt

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.state
signals.functionality: Combinationally computes the arbiter's next state using the current arbiter state, core request start conditions and system response ack signals.
role: computed from inputs and current state
signals.evidence: arbiter_nxt <= arbiter default; case arbiter.state branches assign arbiter_nxt.state in arbiter_comb

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.cmd
signals.functionality: Sets the next AMO opcode combinationally: by default from arbiter, or from core_req_i.amoop when an AMO start condition is met.
signals.evidence: arbiter_nxt <= arbiter default; arbiter_nxt.cmd <= core_req_i.amoop in S_IDLE branch

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.rdata
signals.functionality: Captures sys_rsp_i.data into the arbiter next-state record when in the read-wait state so it can be held for later use.
signals.evidence: arbiter_nxt.rdata <= sys_rsp_i.data in S_READ_WAIT; arbiter_nxt defaulted to arbiter

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.wdata
signals.functionality: Holds the core write data in the next-state record when an AMO starts so it will be captured into the arbiter register on the next clock.
signals.evidence: arbiter_nxt.wdata <= core_req_i.data in S_IDLE; arbiter_nxt defaulted to arbiter

signals.name: alu_res
signals.functionality: Clocked register that stores the ALU result computed from arbiter.rdata and arbiter.wdata (or from compare result) based on arbiter.cmd; that result is used for AMO write requests.
signals.evidence: amo_alu process assigns alu_res from arbiter.* and cmp_res; sys_req_o.data uses alu_res when arbiter.state = S_WRITE

signals.name: cmp_opa
signals.functionality: Combinationally forms a 33-bit operand from arbiter.rdata and arbiter.cmd(3) (sign control). It is used in the signed compare to compute cmp_less and cmp_res.
signals.evidence: cmp_opa <= (arbiter.rdata(arbiter.rdata'left) and arbiter.cmd(3)) & arbiter.rdata; used in signed(...) compare

signals.name: cmp_opb
signals.functionality: Combinationally forms a 33-bit operand from arbiter.wdata and arbiter.cmd(3). It is compared with cmp_opa to produce cmp_less and contributes to cmp_res.
signals.evidence: cmp_opb <= (arbiter.wdata(arbiter.wdata'left) and arbiter.cmd(3)) & arbiter.wdata; used in signed(...) compare

signals.name: cmp_less
signals.functionality: Combinational flag set when signed(cmp_opa) < signed(cmp_opb). It is then used, together with arbiter.cmd(0), to select between operands for cmp_res.
signals.evidence: cmp_less <= '1' when (signed(cmp_opa) < signed(cmp_opb)) else '0'; used in cmp_res

signals.name: cmp_res
signals.functionality: Selects either cmp_opa(31 downto 0) or cmp_opb(31 downto 0) depending on (cmp_less xor arbiter.cmd(0)). This 32-bit result is used by the ALU when command falls through to compare semantics.
signals.evidence: cmp_res <= cmp_opa(31 downto 0) when ((cmp_less xor arbiter.cmd(0)) = '1') else cmp_opb(31 downto 0)

signals.name: state
signals.functionality: Holds the finite-state machine state across clock edges; rvs_control updates it based on core_req_i, rvso and sys_rsp_i.ack, and its bit1 is used to gate sys_req_o.stb and sc_fail logic.
role: provides state bit to combinational logic
signals.evidence: rvs_control: case state is ... (state is case selector); state(1) used in bus_request sys_req_o.stb and in sc_result

signals.name: rvso
signals.functionality: Combinationally indicates the AMO RVS condition when core_req_i.amo is set and amoop(3 downto 2) = "10"; used to gate FSM transitions, sys_req_o.stb and to compute sc_fail.
signals.evidence: rvso <= '1' when (core_req_i.amo = '1') and (core_req_i.amoop(3 downto 2) = "10") else '0'; used in rvs_control and bus_request and sc_result

signals.name: sc_fail
signals.functionality: Captured on the clock from rvso, core_req_i.stb, core_req_i.rw and state(1) to indicate an SC failure; its value modifies core response ack and data.
role: captured from AMO and request signals
signals.evidence: sc_result process: sc_fail <= rvso and core_req_i.stb and core_req_i.rw and (not state(1)) on rising_edge(clk_i)
